classification.difficultyReason: Link polynomial factorisation and real zeroes to value tables and sketches, distinguish crossings from repeated-root contacts, and confirm the symmetry established in Question 6. The quintic requires successive difference-of-squares factorisation and recognising that x²+4 contributes no real zeroes; these are routine linked procedures.

content.prompt: Factor each polynomial below and write down its zeroes (that is, its $x$-intercepts). Then use a table of values to sketch its graph. Graphing software might also be used. Confirm whether the graph has $y$-axis symmetry, origin symmetry or neither.

inlines.text: The zeroes are −3 and 3. One suitable table is shown.
Plot the table points and join with a smooth parabola. Equal values at opposite x-values confirm reflection symmetry in the y-axis, agreeing with the even classification.

spec.description: Upward parabola with intercepts -3,3 and vertex (0,-9).

inlines.text: The zeroes are 1 and 5. One suitable table is shown.
Plot the points and join with a smooth parabola with vertex (3,−4). The graph has neither y-axis symmetry nor origin symmetry, agreeing with the neither classification.

spec.description: Upward parabola crossing at 1 and 5, with y-intercept 5 and labelled vertex (3,-4).

inlines.text: The zeroes are −5, 0 and 5. One suitable table is shown.
Plot the points and draw a smooth cubic through the three zeroes. Opposite x-values give opposite function values, confirming origin symmetry and the odd classification.

spec.description: Cubic with three crossings and origin symmetry.

inlines.text: The zeroes are −2, 0 and 2. The zero at 0 is repeated. One suitable table is shown.
Plot the points, crossing at −2 and 2 and touching the x-axis at 0. Equal values at opposite x-values confirm y-axis symmetry and the even classification.

spec.description: Even quartic with crossings at ±2 and a tangent contact at the origin.

inlines.text: The zeroes are −5 and 0. The zero at 0 is repeated. One suitable table is shown.
Plot the points, crossing at −5 and touching at 0. Since f(−1)=4 and f(1)=6, the graph has neither y-axis symmetry nor origin symmetry, agreeing with the neither classification.

spec.description: Cubic crossing at -5 and touching at the origin, with both turning points retained.

answer.short: $f(x)=x(x-2)(x+2)(x^2+4)$. Real zeroes $-2,0,2$. Odd, with origin symmetry.

inlines.text: Since x²+4 is positive for real x, the real zeroes are −2, 0 and 2. One suitable table is shown.
Plot the points and draw a smooth curve through the three zeroes. Opposite x-values give opposite function values, confirming origin symmetry and the odd classification.

spec.description: Odd quintic with crossings at -2,0,2 and two turning points.
